To distinguish between Cl- and HSO4-, I can test the solubility of the precipitate in ammonia:
- AgCl dissolves in dilute ammonia to form [Ag(NH3)2]+

Interesting! A white precipitate also formed with Ba(NO3)2. This could indicate sulfate (BaSO4) or possibly chloride (BaCl2 is soluble, so this shouldn't precipitate).

Wait - BaCl2 is soluble, so this precipitate must be BaSO4, indicating the presence of sulfate (HSO4-).

But I also got a precipitate with AgNO3. Let me reconsider:
- If the anion is HSO4-, then:
  - With AgNO3: Ag2SO4 forms (white, slightly soluble)
  - With Ba(NO3)2: BaSO4 forms (white, insoluble)

- If the anion is Cl-, then:
  - With AgNO3: AgCl forms (white, insoluble)
  - With Ba(NO3)2: BaCl2 is soluble, no precipitate should form

Since I got precipitates with BOTH AgNO3 and Ba(NO3)2, this strongly suggests the anion is HSO4- (or SO4²-).
